note: Package versions this repository refuses to resolve. Each entry names a published release known to carry an install-time payload, with the campaign that published it and the advisory the judgement rests on. A version is listed because a source says it is malicious, never because it looks suspicious: the guard fails a build on a match, so a guess here is an outage. Refresh from the trackers named under each campaign when they publish updates, and add the campaign rather than folding new versions into an existing one.

keyv-cacheable-2026-08.summary: Trojanized releases of keyv and the cacheable helper family. A preinstall script steals credentials from the machine and from CI, and republishes the payload into further packages.
